internal.talk_track: Put a Sessionboard station in every room: the decks are already there, the captions are on the monitor, and you can see from your desk which rooms are up.

draft.docs_gap: Help Center article and training chapter 68 are live; the stations list ships in web-ui-v2 #1347 (listed above, so the entry stays unannounced until it is in production).

entries.title: Registration Type step: promo codes, Remove and screen-reader labels
entries.summary: On the registration form's **Type** step, a promo code that opens another ticket now clears a choice that no longer exists, and **Continue** waits until the registrant picks one, so the quote always matches the pick. **Remove** after **Join and register** returns a non-member to the ticket they picked (for example **Non-member · VIP**) instead of **Free**, and screen readers announce each option with its type and ticket ("Student · VIP").

where.path: Registration → [registration form] → Type step

entries.use_case: Events with member pricing or promo codes that unlock tickets get the quote the registrant actually chose, and registrants using a screen reader can tell the options apart.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a promo code causes the wrong ticket to appear on a quote, that clicking Remove after joining drops someone to Free, or that a screen reader reads all radio buttons as the same label on the Type step.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration (beta) with promo codes that unlock additional ticket types, or with member/non-member pricing tiers.
internal.gotchas: Registrant-facing only; the admin and API halves of the same sweep are separate entries.
internal.talk_track: If a registrant enters a promo code and then hits Continue without re-selecting a type, they used to get a quote missing both ticket IDs. Now the form clears the stale selection and keeps Continue disabled until they pick a valid option. The Remove-lands-on-Free bug and the screen-reader label issue are fixed in the same release.

entries.title: Registration admin: registration webhooks, decline reasons, cancel emails, comp badge and import time zones
entries.summary: **Webhooks** can subscribe to registration and order events (created, confirmed, updated, waitlisted, declined, canceled, transferred, checked in; order paid and refunded). Declining a registration opens **Decline registration** with your preset reasons and emails the registrant **Registration declined** with the reason. Canceling from the drawer emails **Registration canceled** unless you untick it; buyers who only register others get **Order confirmation (buyer)**; every registration email uses your **Reply-to**. Comp orders show a **Comp** badge with the reason in the order drawer, bulk-update imports read times without a zone in the event's time zone, new Presenter and Exhibitor staff forms start with an invitation code, and archiving a pass quota asks first.

where.path: Registration → Registrants; Registration → Orders; Registration → Messages; Registration → Forms; Registration → Settings; Settings → Integrations → Webhooks

entries.use_case: Event teams using Registration can now receive real-time webhook notifications when registrations are created, updated, or canceled and when orders are paid or refunded — enabling live sync to CRMs, data warehouses, or custom automations without polling. Staff managing approvals get a structured decline flow with preset reasons that appear in the registrant's decline email, reducing back-and-forth with rejected applicants.

cs_action.note: Wallet switch will show 'not set up on this platform yet' until Apple/Google Wallet credentials are configured in Doppler prod-us — coordinate with Josh before surfacing wallet features to customers. internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about real-time registration data sync, approval workflows with automated decline emails, or reports that comp-reason badges, Reply-to addresses, or QR codes in Gmail were missing.

The approval decline flow now captures a reason that goes straight into the registrant's email, and comp orders show their reason right in the order drawer.

entries.use_case: Exhibitor-facing workflows that were silently broken — missing deadlines, failed agreement sends, wrong badge counts, purchases landing on the wrong account, and invoices never emailed — now work end-to-end without staff intervention. Verify with any customer actively using Expo booth sales, exhibitor portals, or floor-map booth assignments that their deadlines, badge allotments, and invoices now appear correctly. entries.title: Registrant drawer now shows add-on, membership and group answers, and file questions display correctly

entries.title: Attend app activity feeds more Pathways Signals — session views, speaker views, notes, declines, walk-in check-ins and live caption watches

entries.title: Sign in to the Help Center with your Sessionboard account

internal.talk_track: The Submission PDF now opens right in the review page.

entries.title: Housing status shows in the drawer for registrants added by staff
entries.summary: The **Housing** line in a registrant's drawer (booked or cancelled, hotel, dates, reference) now shows for every registration your housing provider reported on, including registrations added by staff or imported, not only those placed on a registration form.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → [registrant]

entries.use_case: Staff answering "did this person book a room?" see it in the registrant's drawer instead of going to Integrations & API → Housing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the housing hand-off says the drawer shows no Housing line for a registrant the Housing panel lists as booked.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on Registration (beta) who use the housing hand-off (Passkey or another provider).
internal.gotchas: The line appears only after the provider has posted a status for that registration.
internal.talk_track: Every registrant your housing provider reports on now shows the booking in their drawer, however they were registered.

entries.title: Notifications show recent deliveries and the result of each Test
entries.summary: Under **Registration → Settings → Notifications**, **Recent deliveries** is always shown below the rules and lists the last 25 messages sent and any that failed (it was a collapsed line before). Each **Test** button now keeps its result next to it: sent, or the reason it was not.

where.path: Registration → Settings → Notifications

entries.use_case: Organizers can see what their notification rules sent and confirm a test went out without checking the inbox first.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether their registration notifications are being sent, or says Test did nothing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on Registration (beta) who set up staff notification rules.
internal.gotchas: Test messages are not listed under Recent deliveries; that list is real registration notifications only.
internal.talk_track: The Notifications card now lists what it sent and shows each test's result right next to the button.

entries.title: Receipts show the buyer's VAT number, and euro PDFs show €
entries.summary: A paid registration order downloads as a receipt. The receipt now prints the buyer's VAT number under their email, as the invoice does; before, it printed the reverse-charge note without the number. Invoices, receipts and statements in euros print **€** where they printed **?**.

where.path: Registration checkout confirmation → Download receipt; attendee portal → Tickets & receipts

entries.use_case: A business buyer charged no VAT under the reverse charge needs their own VAT number on the document they keep. Their receipt now carries it, including after they pay an invoice.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an EU customer, or one of their registrants, asks why a receipt has the reverse-charge note but no VAT number.
internal.who_should_get_it: Registration customers who collect VAT numbers (Settings → Tax).
internal.staff_path: Registration → Orders → [paid order] → View as registrant → Tickets & receipts
internal.gotchas: Only buyers who entered a VAT number at checkout get the VAT line. Invoices already showed it (SB-10645). No EUR registration orders exist in prod yet, so no customer has received a PDF with "?" amounts.
internal.talk_track: Receipts now print the buyer's VAT number, the same as invoices, so a paid reverse-charge order still has a complete VAT document.

entries.title: Import translated values for standard contact fields
entries.summary: With a language variant switched on, the contact import now offers a column per language for standard fields such as **First Name**, **Last Name**, **Company** and **Job Title**, not only for custom fields.

where.path: Contacts → Options → Import → Map Columns

entries.use_case: Multilingual events can load translated names and job titles for hundreds of speakers in one import instead of typing each one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a multilingual event asks how to bulk-load translated speaker names.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with language variants on contact fields (Tahaluf).
internal.gotchas: Email and Headshot URL never take a variant column; org-level imports have none (variants are event-scoped).
internal.talk_track: Turn on the variant for the field, then the import template has a column for each language.

entries.title: Edit translated first and last names on a contact
entries.summary: When **First Name**, **Last Name**, **Salutation** or **Honorific** has a language variant, a globe now appears beside the contact's name, and each name field in the name editor has its own globe for its translations.

where.path: Contacts → contact → name at the top of the profile

entries.use_case: Teams on multilingual events can keep each speaker's name in every language on the record itself.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says the globe is missing on First Name or Last Name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with language variants on contact name fields.
internal.staff_path: Contacts → open a contact → click the name
internal.gotchas: The globe sits in the name editor because the name fields are not in the field list.
internal.talk_track: Click the name; each translated name field has its own globe.

entries.title: Converting a session to a subsession follows the parent participant setting
entries.summary: **Convert Submissions** and **Assign to Parent Session** now follow **Participants shown on the parent session**: **None** adds nobody to the parent, **Presenting author only** adds just the primary speaker, **All** adds everyone as before.

where.path: Session → Connections → Convert Submissions; Sessions → Assign to Parent Session

entries.use_case: Parents of grouped sessions list only the people the event wants shown, instead of every subsession participant.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says converted subsessions copy all their participants to the parent.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using subsessions with the setting at None or Presenting author only.
internal.staff_path: Program → Settings → Agenda → Participants shown on the parent session
internal.gotchas: Existing parents are not changed; only new conversions follow the setting.
internal.talk_track: Set the agenda setting once and conversions follow it.

entries.title: Require secure links on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Website
entries.summary: The standard contact fields **LinkedIn URL**, **X (Twitter) URL**, **Facebook URL** and **Website** now offer **Require secure links (https://)**, so links entered with `http://` are saved as `https://`.

where.path: Settings → Fields → People → LinkedIn URL

entries.use_case: Keeps speaker social links consistent and secure without changing the fields or their existing data.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants social links forced to https.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers that publish speaker social links (Clarion Enlit).
internal.staff_path: Settings → Fields → People → field → Require secure links
internal.gotchas: The fields keep their Text type; links already saved keep their address until edited.
internal.talk_track: Tick Require secure links on the field.

entries.title: Lite events show a clear message when you are not on the event team
entries.summary: Opening a Lite event you are not on the team of now shows the standard *not on this event's team* page instead of a red error for every request. Sessionboard staff are given access as on standard events.

where.path: Organization → Events → a Lite event

entries.use_case: Admins see why a Lite event will not open and who to ask, instead of a wall of errors.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports 403 errors opening a Lite event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations using Lite events.
internal.gotchas: The fix for the customer is to add them to the event team (Org Settings → Team).
internal.talk_track: Add the person to the event team and the event opens.

entries.title: A participant lookup that cannot run shows a clear message
entries.summary: When a submission form's participant lookup cannot reach its verification service, submitters now see the rule's message (or *the verification service could not be reached*) instead of *Internal Server Error*.

where.path: Submission form → Participants step → Continue

entries.use_case: Submitters know the check could not run and can try again, and staff can see which rule failed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a submitter reports Internal Server Error on the participants step.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with participant validation rules (ASA, OLC).
internal.gotchas: The check fails closed: the submitter cannot continue while the service is down.
internal.talk_track: The message now says the check could not run.

entries.title: Answer rules on an option no longer hide a same-named option with different case
entries.summary: An answer rule on **Tag A** now hides only **Tag A**, not a different option called **tag a**.

where.path: Submission form → Tags

entries.use_case: Options whose names differ only in capitals behave independently on forms.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says a rule hides the wrong tag.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with answer rules on tags or dropdowns.
internal.staff_path: Form editor → field → Rules → answer options
internal.gotchas: Case-insensitive matching still applies when no option spells the rule text exactly.
internal.talk_track: Each option's rule now applies to that option only.

entries.title: Exhibitor and sponsor contacts work on every plan
entries.summary: Adding a contact to an exhibitor or sponsor company no longer needs **Exhibitor Pro** or **Sponsor Pro**: the profile's **Contacts**, **Create & Add Contacts** and the **No Primary Contacts** tab work on every plan, so Groups Advocacy has someone to email. Portal login stays part of Pro. A failed add now says why instead of showing **Error**.

where.path: CRM → Exhibitors / Sponsors → [company] → CRM → Contacts

entries.use_case: An event without Exhibitor Pro can still give each exhibitor its people, so Email exhibitors in an Advocacy campaign and agreements to the primary contact reach a real person.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A non-Pro customer cannot add contacts to a company, or Groups Advocacy has nobody to email.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Exhibitors or Sponsors but without the Pro modules.
internal.gotchas: Without Pro, contacts get no portal login and Manage Portal Access stays disabled.
internal.talk_track: Contacts are CRM data and work on every plan; Pro is the exhibitor and sponsor portal.

entries.title: Expo Sales tile shows booths sold
entries.summary: On the event Dashboard, **Your toolkit → Expo Sales** now reads **In use** once booth sales are on and a floor plan has booths, with booths sold as its count, instead of **Ready to start / Build your floor plan**. The German tile text now uses *du* like the other tiles.

where.path: Event → Dashboard → Your toolkit

entries.use_case: Teams already selling booths see Expo Sales counted as in use with their booths sold, so the toolkit's adoption count is right.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why Expo Sales says Ready to start while they sell booths.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Expo Sales (floor maps and booth sales) on.
internal.gotchas: With Floor Maps on and booth sales off, the tile still reads Ready to start.
internal.talk_track: The tile now counts booths sold, the same number as Expo › Overview.

entries.title: Booth applications show an estimated total and carry the website
entries.summary: On the Exhibit & sponsor page, an application's Review step now reads **Estimated total** and says the final price follows the booth your team assigns; direct purchases and sponsor-only applications are charged exactly the total shown. Approving an application (or a direct purchase that creates the company) now also saves the website the exhibitor entered on the CRM account.

where.path: Exhibit & sponsor page → Review; Expo → Booth sales → Applications → Approve

entries.use_case: Exhibitors are told up front that an application's price follows the assigned booth, and new exhibitor accounts arrive with their website filled in.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An exhibitor says they were invoiced more than the page showed after a booth was assigned.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events selling booths through applications.
internal.gotchas: An existing account keeps its own website; a website over 255 characters is not copied.
internal.talk_track: Applications show an estimate because the booth is assigned later; direct purchases charge the shown total.

entries.title: Save any step of the Awards program wizard, and no more lost changes on the way out
entries.summary: Every step of the Awards program setup wizard now has a **Save** button beside **Continue**: it saves the step, keeps you on it, and confirms with **Saved**. Leaving with **Back to program** while a step has unsaved changes now asks **Save and leave**, **Leave without saving**, or **Stay on this step**, and the browser warns before a reload or tab close.

where.path: Awards → Programs → [program] → Settings (every wizard step)

entries.use_case: Admins building a long nomination form can save as they go without stepping forward and back, and can no longer lose questions they added by leaving the wizard before clicking Continue.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says questions or settings they added in the Awards wizard disappeared (Informa CPHI, Oct 30), or asks how to save the form without moving on.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Awards customer.
internal.gotchas: The Customize Question dialog's Save only updates the form being built; the step is stored by Save or Continue. Save is enabled once the step has unsaved changes and passes the same checks as Continue.
internal.talk_track: Changes on a wizard step are kept until you save the step. Use Save to store it without moving on; if you try to leave with unsaved changes, the wizard now asks first.

entries.title: Edit Awards pricing rules in place and change their order
entries.summary: On the Awards wizard's **Pricing** step, click a rule's pencil to open it with its current values and **Save Rule** without deleting it, and use the up and down arrows to reorder rules. Rules apply from top to bottom, so a **Set fee to** rule replaces what the rules above it produced; the order is saved and the fee is calculated in it.

where.path: Awards → Programs → [program] → Settings → Pricing → Pricing Rules

entries.use_case: Programs with layered pricing (category fees, member discounts) can fix a rule or arrange the order the fees apply without rebuilding rules from scratch.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer has several pricing rules and asks how to change one, or why a discount is not applying after a Set fee to rule.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers that collect fees.
internal.gotchas: Existing programs keep the order their rules were created in. Moving a Set fee to rule below an Add or Subtract rule changes the fee.
internal.talk_track: Rules now apply top to bottom in the order you see; use the arrows to arrange them and the pencil to change one.

entries.title: Review Only rounds no longer show Apply Now on your Site
entries.summary: Your Site's program list no longer shows Review Only rounds, so submitters are not offered **Apply Now** on a round that takes no new submissions.

where.path: Site → Open Programs

entries.use_case: Programs with a finalist or second Review Only round stop collecting stray applications against it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports Apply Now on a second round (AMA, Oct 23).
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with more than one round.
internal.gotchas: Drafts already started from a Review Only round stay as normal drafts in the program.
internal.talk_track: Review Only rounds are for scoring entries that advanced; your Site now only lists rounds that take submissions.

entries.title: Site forms accept a link typed without https://
entries.summary: URL questions on Site submission forms accept a link with or without `https://` (it is saved as `https://`), and a value that is not a web link, such as `ftp://…`, is refused with a message before submit instead of being saved empty.

where.path: Site → [program] → submission form → URL questions

entries.use_case: Nominators no longer get a browser error for typing example.com, and nobody's link is silently dropped.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a submitter reports 'Please enter a URL' on a nomination or interest form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose forms have URL questions.
internal.gotchas: Applies to Awards, Interest Form and speaker URL questions on Sites.
internal.talk_track: Type the link however you like; the form saves it as https://.

entries.title: Individual Reviewer assignment works on Interest Form review plans
entries.summary: On Interest Form review plans, **Assignments → Individual Reviewer** now assigns the reviewers you tick to every submission in scope, with a matching preview, instead of failing.

where.path: CRM → Interest Forms → [form] → Review → [plan] → Assignments

entries.use_case: Admins can hand specific submissions' review to named reviewers on Interest Forms, as they can on event plans.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports Assign does nothing with Individual Reviewer on an Interest Form plan.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Interest Form review plans.
internal.gotchas: The reviewers must be enrolled on the round.
internal.talk_track: Pick Individual Reviewer, tick the reviewers, and they are assigned to every submission in the scope you chose.

entries.title: Add to Event from an Interest Form submission's panel
entries.summary: **… → Add to Event** in an Interest Form submission's side panel now opens with that submission selected, so you can pick an event and assign it without going back to the table.

where.path: CRM → Interest Forms → [form] → Submissions → [submission] → … → Add to Event

entries.use_case: Admins reviewing one submission can place it in an event from the same panel.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports '0 selected submissions' in Add to Event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Interest Forms with events.
internal.gotchas: Submissions already in an event keep Add to Event disabled.
internal.talk_track: Open the submission, choose Add to Event from the … menu, pick the event.

entries.title: Public registration form: event-time closing date, header image, no empty pages, Full label
entries.summary: The public form shows **Opens** and **Closes** in the event's time zone wherever the visitor is, shows the form's **Header image URL**, skips a page with no questions for the registrant, and a form filled by **Close at this many registrations** reads **Full** in the Forms list and on the public registration page. Country names, **Choose…** and the footer follow the registrant's language.

where.path: The event Site's registration pages; Registration → Forms

entries.use_case: Registrants abroad see the real deadline, the form carries the organizer's header image, and organizers can tell a full form from one whose window ended.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a wrong closing time for visitors in another country, a missing header image, an empty page step, or a 'Closed (window ended)' label on a capped form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Registration (beta).
internal.gotchas: The admin 'Full' label needs the web-api release that adds closed_reason; until then a capped form reads 'Closed'.
internal.talk_track: The public form now reads its window in the event's time zone, shows your header image, and skips pages with nothing to answer.

entries.title: Workshop picking rules: find sessions by title; Import prices remove also leaves the slot
entries.summary: **Edit rules** on the Workshops page stays usable with hundreds of Program sessions: lists start with the sessions that matter, 40 at a time, with **Find a session by title** and each session's time and price. A workshop taken out with **Import prices** `remove` also leaves its slot, so it is no longer offered as a free pick.

where.path: Registration → Workshops → Picking rules → Edit rules; Import prices

entries.use_case: Events with large programs can set up workshop slots without the dialog running off-screen, and removing a paid workshop never turns it into a free one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with a large program says Edit rules is slow or its controls are off-screen, or a removed workshop still shows on the form.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers selling workshops through Registration (beta).
internal.gotchas: With List free sessions on, every public Program session is a free pick by design; hide a removed workshop with its Hidden rule.
internal.talk_track: Search the session list in Picking rules, and a removed workshop is gone from the form.

entries.title: Deleted resource pages leave every portal, and page changes are in the Audit log
entries.summary: Deleting a **Resources** page now removes it from every portal straight away, so portal users no longer see a link that opens "not found". A restore from Trash puts it back where it was, even if the portal was saved in the meantime. Creating, editing, duplicating and deleting a page are recorded in **History → Audit** as **Portal page**.

where.path: Program → Portals → Resources

entries.use_case: Admins can see who created or deleted a portal page, and participants never land on a deleted one.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says a deleted portal page still shows in the portal, or asks who deleted a page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using portal Resources pages.
internal.staff_path: History → Deleted → Portal page → Restore (staff only)
internal.gotchas: Restore is staff-only; Audit rows start from this release (no backfill).
internal.talk_track: Deleting a page now takes it out of every portal at once, and the Audit log shows who did it.

entries.title: Portal session edit counts combined-limit fields the portal hides
entries.summary: In the portal's session panel, the counter for a combined character limit now adds up every field in the rule, including fields the portal's **Show/Hide fields** leave out, so a submission already over the limit reads over the limit instead of **0**.

where.path: Portal → My Participation → session → Edit

entries.use_case: Submitters see the true combined total for an abstract even when some of its fields are not editable in the portal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a submitter reports the combined counter reading 0 in the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using combined character limits on submission forms.
internal.staff_path: Session form → Character limit rules; Portal → session → Edit
internal.gotchas: Needs the web-api release that sends stored_lengths; older API keeps the old count.
internal.talk_track: The portal counter now matches what the server enforces.

entries.title: Imported floor plans publish, and the designer frees or protects sold booths
entries.summary: Booths that only touch after a DXF, ExpoFP, Map Your Show or eShow import no longer count as overlapping, so an imported plan can be published. Setting a booth to **Available** in the designer clears its exhibitor and hold, and is refused while an application holds the booth. Deleting a map or hall removes its booths from Booth sales, and is refused while a booth on it is held, reserved or sold. Map settings stays open while a CAD drawing imports.

where.path: Expo → Floor plan → [map] → Inspector / Audit / Map settings; Floor Maps → Map actions → Delete

entries.use_case: Publish a plan imported from last year's vendor without nudging booths, and never resell a booth that still has an order.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an imported plan will not publish ("Fix audit errors"), a booth set to Available still shows its exhibitor, or a deleted map still counts in Booth sales.
internal.who_should_get_it: Expo Sales customers using the floor-map designer, especially those importing from ExpoFP, Map Your Show, eShow or CAD.
internal.staff_path: Expo → Floor plan → an imported map → Audit; Inspector → Status
internal.gotchas: A booth on a live exhibitor application must be released in Booth sales first; the designer says so. Real overlaps (two imports stacked on each other) still block Publish.
internal.talk_track: Imported plans publish straight away, and the designer can no longer resell a booth that has an order.

entries.title: The exhibit page booth picker covers every published map and hall
entries.summary: On the Exhibit & sponsor page, the Booth step now offers every hall of every published floor map, with hall tabs on the map and every booth in the list and the available count. Each booth shows its type from the designer and its size in square feet, and held booths read **On hold** instead of sold.

where.path: Program Site: /s/<slug>/exhibit/<event ID> → Booth step

entries.use_case: Sell booths across several halls and maps from one exhibit page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an organizer with more than one hall or floor map says exhibitors can only see one of them.
internal.who_should_get_it: Expo Sales customers with multi-hall or multi-map floor plans.
internal.gotchas: Square feet need the hall scale set (Calibrate scale) in the designer.
internal.talk_track: Exhibitors can now pick a booth in any hall, on any published map.

entries.title: Registration emails show in History, and confirmations carry the receipt
entries.summary: Every registration email (confirmations, waitlist, approval, cancellation, reminders and the buyer's order confirmation) now appears in **History → Emails → Sent Emails**, and one the mail provider refuses appears under **Errors**. Confirmations and the buyer's order confirmation attach the order's receipt as a PDF (an invoice while unpaid); a colleague registered by someone else never gets the buyer's receipt.

where.path: History → Emails → Sent Emails / Errors; Registration → Emails & SMS

entries.use_case: Organizers can prove a registrant was emailed, see a failed confirmation the same day, and stop answering "where is my receipt?" because the receipt arrives with the confirmation.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether a registrant got their confirmation, or a registrant asks for their receipt.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Registration.
internal.staff_path: Event → History → Emails → Sent Emails (search the registrant's address)
internal.gotchas: Only registration emails sent after this release are listed; earlier ones were never recorded. Registration rows show sent or refused, not opens or clicks, and the copy has the registrant's portal links removed. Anonymising a registrant clears their copies. Free orders get a $0 receipt. Goes live with the next web-api production release.
internal.talk_track: Registration emails are now in History like every other email, failures included, and the confirmation carries the receipt the thank-you page promises.

entries.title: Registration emails: correct time zone, readable claim-by time, waitlist position and changed fields
entries.summary: The **When** line uses the time zone in force on the event's date (PST for a December event in Los Angeles), **A seat opened up** shows the claim-by time as a date and time in the event's zone, **Waitlisted** always says the registrant's position, and **Registration changed** names only the fields whose value changed.

where.path: Registration → Emails & SMS

entries.use_case: Registrants get emails that read correctly: the right time zone, a claim-by time they can act on, their place on the waitlist, and a change email that lists only what they changed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a wrong PDT/PST label, a raw timestamp such as 2026-10-29T20:35:13Z in a waitlist email, or a change email listing fields the registrant did not touch.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Registration.
internal.gotchas: A portal edit that changes nothing no longer sends a Registration changed email. Goes live with the next web-api production release.
internal.talk_track: The registration emails now read correctly: right time zone, readable claim-by time, waitlist position and only the fields that changed.

entries.title: Disclosures export leaves out mitigations for roles without Credits
entries.summary: The Disclosures export now includes the **Mitigation**, **Mitigation Notes**, **Mitigation Decided By** and **Mitigation Decided At** columns only for people whose role can open the **Mitigations** tab (the **Credits** permission). Everyone else with Disclosures access gets the same file without them.

where.path: Contacts → Disclosures → Requests or Mitigations → Export

entries.use_case: Teams can give staff Disclosures access without also handing them faculty mitigation decisions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer limits who sees mitigation decisions, or asks why an export has no mitigation columns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Disclosures with Credits.
internal.staff_path: Org → Settings → Roles → Credits permission; Contacts → Disclosures → Export
internal.gotchas: An export without mitigation columns means the requester's role lacks Credits read, not missing data.
internal.talk_track: Mitigation decisions now follow the Credits permission everywhere, including the export.

entries.title: Disclosure reminders with a one-day cadence no longer skip days
entries.summary: With **Remind every (days)** set to **1**, an open disclosure request is now reminded on every daily run until it reaches three reminders. Before, some days were skipped, so a one-day cadence sometimes behaved like two.

where.path: Contacts → Disclosures → Settings → Remind every (days)

entries.use_case: Short request windows get the daily nudges they were set up for.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a missing disclosure reminder on a day it was due.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Disclosures reminders.
internal.gotchas: Reminders go out once a day at 13:15 UTC; a request sent later in the day is first reminded on the next day's run or the one after.
internal.talk_track: A one-day cadence now means every day.

entries.title: Portal sidebar shows how many contracts are waiting for you
entries.summary: In a Site's portal, **My Contracts** in the sidebar now shows the number of agreements waiting for the signed-in person's signature, the same count as the **Needs Signature** tab.

where.path: Site portal → sidebar → My Contracts

entries.use_case: Speakers and sponsor contacts see at a glance that an agreement needs them, without opening the page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer turns on My Contracts in their portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Contracts with the portal My Contracts widget.
internal.staff_path: Event → Site → Portal → Home → Portal widgets → My Contracts
internal.gotchas: The badge shows only when the My Contracts widget is on and the org has Contracts.
internal.talk_track: The sidebar now tells signers they have something to sign.

entries.title: Claim-site evaluations refuse answers outside a question's scale
entries.summary: An evaluation submitted with a claim, a lesson's evaluation step or a survey link now refuses an answer outside its question's range, such as 9 on a 1–5 scale, so Survey Results and accreditation reports only count valid answers.

where.path: Claim site → Claim → evaluation

entries.use_case: Evaluation means stay valid for accreditation reporting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sees an impossible mean (above the scale) in a survey's Results.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Credit Claiming or Surveys.
internal.gotchas: Answers stored before this release are unchanged; an earlier out-of-range answer still counts until removed.
internal.talk_track: Out-of-range answers can no longer reach your results.

entries.title: Submission forms sign people in by magic link when passwords are off
entries.summary: On an event that signs portal users in by **Magic link** with **Username & password** off, the submission form's account step now asks for an email and offers **Email me a sign-in link**. The link brings the person back to the form signed in; someone new gives their name first and their account is created when they open the link. Before, these forms showed only "Insufficient event authentication methods detected".

where.path: Public submission form → Account step (when Settings → Portal Login has Username & password off and Magic link on)

entries.use_case: Events that use passwordless sign-in can now take submissions without turning passwords back on: submitters get an emailed link that returns them to the form.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer on magic-link-only portal sign-in reports that their submission form says 'Insufficient event authentication methods detected'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Username & password off and Magic link on (four live events on 2026-10-30, including ODA Annual Spring Meeting 2027).
internal.gotchas: The link proves who the person is; portal access still comes with the submission. External-user validation (allowlists) still applies.

entries.title: Turn portal account creation on or off yourself
entries.summary: **Settings → Portal Login** has a new switch, **New people can create an account**, for whether someone without an account may create one from the portal sign-in page. It used to need a request to Support.

enable.path: Event → Settings → Portal Login → New people can create an account

where.path: Event → Settings → Portal Login

entries.use_case: Open events can let new speakers or contributors create their own portal account without waiting on Support; closed events keep it off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks Support to turn on portal signup for an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizers running open calls where new people should reach the portal on their own.
internal.staff_path: Same switch; staff no longer need a database change.
internal.gotchas: Off by default. It is not a sign-in method, so it does not count toward the one method that must stay on.

entries.title: SAML sign-in checks that the assertion is addressed to Sessionboard
entries.summary: Sessionboard now refuses a SAML assertion whose **Audience** is not the configuration's SP entity ID (**Issuer URL**, or the **Audience** override), even when its signature is valid. New SAML configurations check it from the first sign-in; existing ones are switched on once their provider's Audience is confirmed to match.

where.path: Org Settings → Enterprise SSO → SAML configuration

entries.use_case: Closes a gap a security review would flag: an assertion your identity provider signed for another application can no longer sign someone in to Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: Existing IdPs are observed, not enforced; Engineering switches each on after its recorded audience matches.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Security questionnaires about SAML assertion validation; a new SAML setup whose test sign-in fails with 'audience mismatch'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organization using SAML SSO.
internal.gotchas: A new configuration whose IdP app has the wrong Audience URI fails sign-in with 'SAML assertion audience mismatch' (Sync Doctor: sso_audience_mismatch). Fix the Audience URI / SP Entity ID in the IdP app.

enable.path: Org Settings → Enterprise SSO (new SAML configurations check it from the first sign-in)

entries.title: Badges print names in Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, Japanese and Korean
entries.summary: Printed badge PDFs now show names and organizations in the registrant's own script. Arabic and Hebrew print right to left with their letters joined, Chinese, Japanese and Korean print in full, and accented Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters such as Ł, ő or Ж no longer drop out. Before, these characters printed as blank space. Batch prints, single prints, reprints, station prints and kiosk prints all use the same renderer.

where.path: Registration → Badges → Print badges; Registrants → Print badge; Onsite desk and stations

entries.use_case: International events can print badges for every attendee without retyping names in Latin letters or hand-writing blank badges at the desk.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with international attendees reports blank names on printed badges.
internal.who_should_get_it: Registration customers with attendees whose names use Arabic, Hebrew, Chinese, Japanese, Korean or accented letters.
internal.gotchas: Text in these scripts is drawn as shapes, so it prints but cannot be selected or searched in the PDF. ZPL (thermal Zebra) output depends on the printer's own fonts and is unchanged. Scripts such as Devanagari or Thai still print blank. Folded table tents and seating charts are not covered yet.
internal.talk_track: Every attendee's name now prints in their own language on the badge.

entries.title: Editing a registration's ticket can no longer oversell a full ticket or shared pool
entries.summary: Picking a ticket in a registrant's **Edit** form, or in a **Bulk update** CSV import, now follows the same capacity rule as new orders and **Change ticket**. A full ticket, or one in a full shared capacity pool, is refused with "… is sold out." and the registration keeps its ticket. Canceled and declined registrations hold no seat, so their ticket can still be changed.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → [registrant] → Edit → Ticket; Registrants → Import CSV → Bulk update

entries.use_case: A ticket's capacity or a shared pool's limit now holds no matter which staff screen moves someone onto it, so a room can't be overbooked from the Edit form.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why an edit was refused as sold out, or reports a ticket showing more sold than its capacity.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration (beta) with capped tickets or shared capacity pools.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Registrants → [registrant] → Edit → Ticket; Registrants → Import CSV → Bulk update
internal.gotchas: Edit never re-prices the order; Change ticket does. Registrations oversold before this fix stay as they are.
internal.talk_track: Staff can still move people between tickets from Edit, but only onto a ticket that has room — exactly like a new order. Use Change ticket when the price difference should be charged or refunded.

entries.title: The registration form says when a ticket goes on sale
entries.summary: A ticket whose sales window has not opened yet is shown greyed out on the public registration form with **On sale from** and the date, in the event's time zone and the registrant's language. A ticket whose window has closed reads **Not on sale**; sold-out tickets read **Sold out**.

where.path: Public registration form → ticket choice

entries.use_case: Registrants see an early-access or later-release ticket coming instead of an unexplained disabled option.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sets a future On sale from date on a ticket and asks what registrants see.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Registration (beta) with sales windows on tickets.
internal.staff_path: Registration → Tickets & pricing → [ticket] → On sale from
internal.gotchas: The date has no time of day; it is the day in the event's time zone.
internal.talk_track: Set On sale from on the ticket; until then the form lists it with the date it opens.

entries.title: One New review assigned email per Assign, listing every submission
entries.summary: When one **Assign** gives a reviewer several submissions, they now get one **New review assigned** email that names all of them (for example "New review assigned: 10 submissions", with the titles listed) and a **Start reviewing** button that opens their queue for that round. Before, they got one email naming a single submission, so reviewers thought they had been assigned one.

where.path: Review plan → Edit → Assignments → Assign

entries.use_case: Reviewers see their whole workload from one email instead of believing they were assigned a single proposal.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says reviewers only got told about one submission.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Review plans.
internal.gotchas: Customized versions of this email keep their own text; for a batch, {{sessionTitle}} reads "N submissions".

shipped.pending: Ships to Prod with the next release cut.

entries.title: Reviewers can read earlier messages when the submitter's portal has messaging off
entries.summary: On the Review portal, a submission whose submitter's portal has **Enable messaging** off now shows the **Messages** section with the earlier messages, read-only, and a note that the submitter can't read new ones. Before, the section disappeared.

where.path: Review portal → My reviews → submission → Messages

entries.use_case: Reviewers keep the context of earlier conversations even after the portal's messaging is turned off.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a reviewer says earlier messages vanished from a submission.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Review plans.
internal.staff_path: Review portal → My reviews → submission → Messages

shipped.pending: Ships to Prod with the next release cut.

entries.title: Reviewer and assignment imports name every bad submission ID in a cell
entries.summary: When a **Submission ID** cell lists several IDs and more than one is wrong or missing, the import's error now names all of them at once, so you fix the row in one go.

where.path: Review plan → Plan Options → Import Assignments / Import Reviewers

entries.use_case: Admins fix a spreadsheet in one pass instead of re-uploading once per bad ID.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an admin says an import only reported one bad Submission ID at a time.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Review plans.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Plan Options → Import Assignments / Import Reviewers

shipped.pending: Ships to Prod with the next release cut.

entries.title: Review plan fixes: assignment success title, one save per round, translated Jump to
entries.summary: The success dialog after **Assign** shows its title ("Submissions successfully assigned to reviewers") in every language instead of a raw key; **Save Changes** on a round sends one save instead of several, and edits made while a save is running are kept; on the Review portal, the **Jump to** filters and list heading and the menu button are translated in French, German and Spanish.

where.path: Review plan → Edit → Rounds / Assignments; Review portal → submission → Jump to

entries.use_case: Cleaner wizard and reviewer experience, especially for non-English teams.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a raw key as the assignment success title, duplicate round saves, or English Jump to labels for French/German reviewers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Review plans.
internal.staff_path: Review plan → Edit → Rounds / Assignments; Review portal → submission → Jump to

shipped.pending: Ships to Prod with the next release cut.

entries.title: Attend admin: Engagement settings open, sponsor creatives upload, busy sends say so
entries.summary: **Attend → Engagement → Settings** opens again (it crashed, so session surveys couldn't be set up). The **Upload** button in the Filestack picker works inside side panels such as **New placement** under Sponsor ads. A notification **Send** that meets a busy server is tried again for a few seconds; if it still can't go, a **Not sent** message shows and the composer stays open.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Engagement → Settings; Attend → Sponsor ads → New placement → Upload; Attend → Notifications → Send

entries.use_case: Organizers can turn on session evaluations, create sponsor placements with a creative, and know when a notification did not go out.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an organizer on the Attend beta reports the Engagement Settings tab crashing, a creative upload that does nothing in Sponsor ads, or a notification that seemed sent but stayed Draft.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend app Early Access beta.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Engagement → Settings; Attend → Sponsor ads → New placement → Upload; Attend → Notifications → Send
internal.gotchas: The picker fix covers every image upload opened from a side panel or dialog, not only sponsor placements.

shipped.pending: Ships to Prod with the next release cut (app: next production app update).

entries.title: Attend app: browse the agenda by room, speaker links, accent-free people search
entries.summary: The agenda's **Browse by** list gains **Room**, and a home button can open the agenda filtered to one room. Speaker profiles list their LinkedIn, X, Facebook and website links. Attendee search in **People** ignores accents (`muller` finds Müller). Recommendations never suggest a Declined session, and the Concierge pack's home shows Sponsors once.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend app → Agenda / People / speaker profile; Attend → Mobile App → Agenda options

entries.use_case: Attendees can find what is next in a room, reach a speaker's profiles, and find people whose names have accents.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an organizer asks for a room filter in the app agenda, speaker LinkedIn links, or says attendees can't find people with accented names.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend app Early Access beta.
internal.staff_path: Attend app → Agenda / People / speaker profile; Attend → Mobile App → Agenda options
internal.gotchas: Speaker links and the Room option in the editor need the web-api release; the app part needs the next production app update.

shipped.pending: Ships to Prod with the next release cut; the app part (sessionboard-mobile#124) with the next production app update.

entries.title: Event dashboard counts time conflicts the way the agenda does
entries.summary: The dashboard's time-conflicts callout now counts only sessions in the same room at the same time, or with the same speaker, chair or moderator in overlapping sessions, the same rule as the agenda's **Conflicts** list. Parallel sessions in different rooms no longer show as conflicts.

where.path: Event → Dashboard → Needs you / Schedule

entries.use_case: Organizers with parallel tracks no longer see every scheduled session flagged as a conflict, so the callout points at real double-bookings.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the dashboard reports most or all of their sessions as conflicting while the agenda's Conflicts list is short.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with multi-track agendas.
internal.gotchas: Ask's dashboard summary uses the same count, and now gives the submission status row with its own total.

entries.title: Ask emails a time block, lists who has not opened an email, and states briefing figures
entries.summary: Ask can build a campaign draft for everyone presenting in a time block, day or room, and list the people who have not opened a campaign email by subject, sender or send date. Briefing replies now state the numbers asked for, report counts no longer change with speaker filters, and the form-layout approval card names standard questions such as Title and Track.

where.path: Ask

entries.use_case: Organizers can reach one block's presenters, chase non-openers and get dashboard numbers straight from Ask without exporting or rebuilding filters.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to email one time block's speakers, who has not opened an email, or why Ask's counts did not match a report.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event using Ask.
internal.gotchas: The agent half ships with the next manual sessionboard-agents PROD publish; the email-open fields need the web-api release.

entries.title: AI-off tooltips tell customers who to contact
entries.summary: When AI features are off for your organization, the tooltips on personas and on the report and dashboard **Describe it** option now say to contact your Sessionboard customer success manager or support, instead of pointing to a settings page only Sessionboard staff can open.

where.path: Program Settings → Personas; Reports → Describe it

entries.use_case: Admins in an organization with AI off know who can turn it on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: An admin in an org with AI off asks how to turn on personas or Describe it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with AI features off.
internal.staff_path: Org Settings → Admin Settings → Enable AI features
internal.gotchas: Staff still see the Admin Settings wording.

entries.title: Revoking a Live Transcribe invite signs out the consoles and stations using it
entries.summary: **Revoke** on a Live Transcribe invite now ends every session already signed in with that link, as well as stopping new sign-ins. A console or **Ready Room** station goes back to the sign-in screen at its next check, within about 30 seconds.

where.path: Marketing → Transcribe → Invites → … → Revoke

entries.use_case: When a crew link is lost or shared too widely, revoking it now cuts off everyone using it straight away, which is what the revoke dialog already promised.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer worries about a crew invite link that was forwarded, lost or used by the wrong vendor.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event running Live Transcribe with invite links or Ready Room stations.
internal.staff_path: Same Revoke action on Marketing → Transcribe → Invites.
internal.gotchas: Before this fix a revoked link only refused new sign-ins; sessions already open kept working for up to 32 hours and kept renewing. A capture already recording keeps its socket until the station's next 30-second check signs it out. Admins signed in with their own login are unaffected.

entries.title: Sessions left out of "Sessions available to transcribe" can't be captured
entries.summary: A session excluded by **Sessions available to transcribe** can no longer be captured from a direct link or a Ready Room station's saved copy. The panel says the session is not available to transcribe, so nothing records.

where.path: Marketing → Transcribe → Settings → Sessions available to transcribe

entries.use_case: Organizers who keep licensed or closed-door sessions out of transcription can rely on the setting: those sessions cannot be recorded by accident, even from an offline station.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer has sessions that must never be recorded (licensed content, closed-door).
internal.who_should_get_it: Events that use the status filter in Sessions available to transcribe.
internal.gotchas: A capture already running when the setting changes is not stopped. Events with no selection (All sessions) are unaffected.

entries.title: Animated caption styles work with uploaded SRT and VTT captions
entries.summary: Clips exported with an **Animated** caption style now show captions when the recording's transcript came from an uploaded SRT or VTT file. Each caption line's words are spaced across the line, and the editor preview shows the same captions.

where.path: Marketing → Media → a recording → Edit & clip → captions

entries.use_case: Teams that bring their own professional captions can now export animated-caption clips for social without re-transcribing the recording.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer uploads SRT/VTT captions and asks why animated clips came out with no captions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone exporting social clips from recordings with uploaded caption files.
internal.gotchas: Caption files have no word timings, so words are spaced evenly across each line rather than matched to speech. AI-transcribed recordings keep exact word timing.

entries.title: Campaign edits save however you leave a step
entries.summary: Changing the message or recipients and then using the top step bar or **Back** now saves the change, so the email that goes out is the one **Preview** showed. **Send** saves anything still unsaved first, and the tab warns before closing on unsaved edits.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → New Campaign / Edit campaign

entries.use_case: Admins who jump between steps with the step bar no longer send an older version of an email they had already corrected and previewed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says a campaign went out with text they had already changed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer that sends Email Campaigns.
internal.gotchas: If a save fails (for example on a sent campaign), the wizard stays on the step and shows the error; Send refuses to go out with unsaved changes.
internal.talk_track: Edits on any step are saved the moment you leave it, by Next, Back or the step bar, and Send double-checks before it goes.

entries.title: Pause and resume recurring campaigns from the campaign list
entries.summary: A scheduled recurring campaign's **…** menu on the campaign list now has **Pause**, and a paused one has **Resume**, next to **Cancel schedule**.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → [recurring campaign] → …

entries.use_case: Admins can stop a weekly reminder for a while without cancelling the series and setting it up again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to hold a recurring send during a quiet period.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with recurring campaigns.
internal.gotchas: Pause applies to recurring campaigns only; one-time scheduled sends still have Cancel schedule.
internal.talk_track: Pause a recurring campaign from the list and resume it when you are ready; nothing sends in between.

entries.title: People campaigns name only the sessions the filter matched
entries.summary: In a **People** campaign filtered by session (for example **Submission status = Accepted**), `{{{sessions_summary}}}` now lists only the matching sessions, and a **Matched session** group in the merge tag picker offers `{{session.title}}`, `{{session.status}}` and the other session fields.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → New Campaign → People → Basic info → Merge tags

entries.use_case: An "accepted" email to speakers no longer lists their pending or declined submissions, and session tags no longer get flagged by the content review.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sends acceptance or logistics emails to people rather than sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers about accepted sessions.
internal.gotchas: With no session filter, session tags are empty and the summary lists every session, as before.
internal.talk_track: Filter a People campaign to accepted sessions and every session tag and summary in the email follows that filter.

entries.title: On/Off switch for system emails that start off
entries.summary: The **File request approved** and **File request denied** emails now show an **On / Off** switch on their row in **Settings → Email Templates → System**, and a **Send this email** switch in the editor, so you can see and change whether they send.

where.path: Settings → Email Templates → System

entries.use_case: Admins can turn the file request decision emails on without editing them, and can tell at a glance whether they are on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to turn on the file request approved or denied emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Portals → File Requests.
internal.gotchas: Saving the editor no longer turns these emails on by itself; use the switch.
internal.talk_track: Flip the switch on the row to start sending the file request emails.

entries.title: Attachment names keep their accents and non-Latin characters
entries.summary: Files attached to campaigns, **Send Email** and email templates now keep names such as `Résumé_日本語.pdf` exactly, in the editor, the preview and the email recipients get.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → New Campaign → Basic info → Attachments

entries.use_case: International events can attach files with accented or non-Latin names without recipients seeing garbled characters.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports garbled attachment names.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with non-English file names.
internal.gotchas: Files uploaded before the fix keep the garbled name; upload them again.
internal.talk_track: Attachment names now arrive exactly as you named the file.

entries.title: Approvals and Contracts screens fully translated
entries.summary: With the admin language set to German, Spanish or French, the Approvals queue, the approval workflow (including **Release time**) and the review drawer are now fully translated, as are the close buttons of every side panel and dialog and the custom-field descriptions in Contracts.

where.path: Event → Approvals; Program → Settings → Files → Edit approval workflow; Contracts → Templates

entries.use_case: Teams working in German, Spanish or French no longer meet English in the approval workflow.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer whose team works in German, Spanish or French uses Approvals or Contracts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with admins in de/es/fr.
internal.gotchas: Dates inside sentences keep the event's date format.
internal.talk_track: Approvals and Contracts now read fully in German, Spanish and French.
